meta.title: The Waiter with One Glove
meta.textType: story: who or what is it?

paragraphs: On Tuesday afternoon, Teacher Kim's class had an English lesson about restaurants. Teacher Kim wrote "Welcome to Our Restaurant" on the blackboard. The letters were big and green. Under the words, she wrote a menu with three dishes. They were fried rice, chicken soup, and banana cake. "Please copy the menu into your notebooks," she said. Lily copied it carefully, but Leo drew a banana.

"Now we will play restaurant," said Teacher Kim. "Leo is the waiter, and Mia and May are the customers." "Lily is the cook." Leo took a white glove and a pencil out of his bag. He put it on his right hand. "A waiter in a big restaurant wears gloves," he said. "But I have only one glove."

"Welcome to our restaurant!" said Leo with a big smile. He gave Mia and May a menu. "Are you ready to order?" he asked. Mia read it first. "I would like fried rice, please," she said. "I will have chicken soup," said May. Leo wrote the order in his notebook. Then he walked to Lily, and he gave her the order. She put some paper food in two paper bowls.

Leo carried the two bowls in his hands, and he began to serve the customers. The glove was too big for him, so it fell into the soup. "Waiter, there is a glove in my soup!" said May. "That is not a problem," said Leo. "It is a special dish for our best customers." Mia laughed so much that she could not eat her rice. The paper food looked delicious, but nobody could eat it.

"Now I need a final customer," said Leo. Teacher Kim sat on a chair at the front of the class. "I would like banana cake, please," she said. Leo brought the cake on a plate. This time, he held the plate with two hands. "Your cake, Teacher Kim," he said. "Please do not look in the soup!" They all laughed, and the lesson ended. It was a funny lesson, and it was a very good one.
